plan_lane.lane_reason: The script is one mechanism being assembled in front of the viewer - a fixed toolbox, then a single machine, then the two things it makes, then the base it stands on - so the argument IS the diagram growing, which is what diagram build does and what icon choreography (a wall of real marks) cannot do for a product nobody has a logo for yet.

law40.law40_letter: LAW 40 binds connectors that EXIST and does not require any.  The plan's first cut ran two terracotta lines from the machine to the two finished tools; the crossed pair then took the WHOLE board (handoff section 9 item 3), which leaves no machine on screen for a line to leave, and a connector to nothing is worse than none.  Every remaining relationship here is CONTAINMENT - the tools in the box, the part on the bed, the machine on the slab - and containment is carried by the declared blocks (LAW 41).  `SC.anchor_points` stays in the module so a lane that later adds a connector cannot hand-place its end.

law42.board_mode_reason: LAW 43: chapters are the default and this script changes subject four times. The toolbox is not modified by the machine - it is REPLACED by it - what the machine makes is its own picture, and the RLM slab with the competing marks is a fourth. Every seam lands on the object the next sentence is about (LAW 45).
law42.note: every board mark carries a finite t_to, which is exactly the declaration LAW 42 asks a CHAPTERED build for, and every one of those t_to values IS a chapter seam.  No single element holds more than 30.5% of the runtime; the MACHINE as an object holds 64.9% across its three instances, which is why all three also carry `data-anchor="1"` and are named in SC.SCENE_ANCHORS.  The only marks that never leave are the four outro ones.
